test_title: PYST 18: SSC CHSL - English (Held On: 7 June 2022 Shift 3)
subject: english
question:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the idiom.

To bite the bullet

options.text: To reject doing something difficult or unpleasant
To be brave in a difficult situation

solution: The correct answer is '**To be brave in a difficult situation**'. [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__** __ • The most appropriate meaning of the given idiom '**To bite the bullet**' is '**To be brave in a difficult situation'**. (कठिन परिस्थिति में बहादुर बनना'।) • **To bite a bullet**: *to force yourself to perform an unpleasant or difficult action or to be brave in a difficult situation (*अपने आप को एक अप्रिय या कठिन कार्य करने के लिए मजबूर करना या कठिन परिस्थिति में बहादुर होना*)* • **E.g.** *I decided I had to bite the bullet and take a couple of math classes even though I knew they were hard.__* • Therefore, as per the points mentioned above, we find the correct answer is **option 3.** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__** __ • Let's look at some similar idioms. • **Be man enough**- *to be brave enough to do something (*कुछ करने के लिए पर्याप्त बहादुर होना*)* • *He was man enough to admit he had made a mistake__*. • **Faint heart never won fair lady**- *timidity will prevent you from achieving your objective (*कायरता आपको अपने लक्ष्य को प्राप्त करने से रोकेगी*)* __ • *Rebecca: Remember that faint heart never won fair lady. He'll probably be flattered and impressed if you approach him first.__* 3a:T838, The correct answer is '**Succesion**'.
